attempts.label: DANDI:001326
attempts.paper_title: Conserved brain-wide emergence of emotional response from sensory experience in humans and mice
attempts.entry_title: Brain-wide mouse electrophysiology during eyepuffs and ketamine (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Most main findings held: ketamine spared fast activity but removed the persistent, accumulating brain-wide response, and it shortened regional decay times while rise times stayed unchanged. The twelve response clusters did not reproduce (11 found, 6 of 12 sizes in range), nor did the stronger ketamine effect on slow clusters, and the clustering shifted with the random seed and BLAS thread count. Partly held: the late emotion-like drop and weaker coupling under ketamine, and the eye-closure reduction, which depends on the code's normalization. Human iEEG persistence, timescale and phase locking were not tested for lack of time. Participant reports, dissociation scores and licking data are absent from the archive.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001326, which holds Neuropixels recordings of 13 sessions from 10 mice during eyepuff and tone series before and after ketamine, and the behavior in dandiset 001347. The first notebook covers the response clusters and their regional distribution, regional rise and decay times, the emotion-like population dimension and its first-order model, the fast and persistent coding dimensions with their baseline timescale and coupling, the tone responses, and the resting correlation structure and spectra. The second covers the eye closure of the recorded mice, the behavior-only mouse drug, dose, pressure and muscimol experiments, and the eye closure of four non-implanted participants, from dandiset 001347. The third covers the human iEEG factor analysis and the network cluster tests, from the derived spectrograms deposited in dandiset 001347.

outcomes.notes: 13 sessions from 10 mice, 9554 curated units, 6698 puff-modulated units (6491 if the code's minimum of 250 is read as spikes). The median session has units in 32 finest-level regions (range 11 to 37; 10 of 13 sessions have at least 24).
deviations: The units in the files are already curated (all labelled good, SNR at least 2.0, at least 517 spikes); the BombCell and ISI criteria cannot be re-applied, as the files hold no waveforms or ISI metrics.

outcomes.notes: With scanpy's default Leiden seed and BLAS on one thread, 11 clusters (within one of 12). In descending order the sizes are 963, 772, 664, 657, 651, 604, 590, 579, 554, 491 and 173; 6 of the 12 expected sizes are within tolerance (the 3rd and the 8th to 11th are not) and there is no 12th (expected 176). By the criterion's measures (code find_decay, absolute values) clusters 9 and 6 are rapid and brief (decay 0.10 and 0.18 s) and two are persistent, cluster 0 (mean |1 to 2 s| 0.26 of the peak, peak at 0.11 s) and cluster 10 (0.42, peak at 0.77 s); the condition of three persistent clusters with two early peaks fails under both numberings. Clusters 1, 4 and 5 decay after 1.35, 1.16 and 1.24 s, with means over 1 to 2 s of 0.22, 0.14 and 0.18 of their peaks. Two of the 11 clusters (0 and 4) are suppressed. Over ten Leiden seeds the count is within 12 +- 1 in 6, 2 to 7 sizes are within tolerance, 0 to 3 clusters are persistent, and the full condition holds in none. The PCA in float64 gives 12 clusters with 7 sizes within tolerance, and the float32 PCA on 4 BLAS threads 11 clusters with 4 within (adjusted Rand index 0.71 against the main partition for both). Changed from partially reproduced after verification round 1: the cluster count holds but the sizes and the persistent structure, the substance of the claim, fail under every seed and both perturbations.
deviations: Leiden runs on the neighbor graph, as scanpy does and as the code calls it, not on the UMAP embedding the Methods name (criterion).
Peak, decay and the |z| < 1 rule follow analysis.py find_decay (plot_cluster_distribution), which works on absolute values; the criterion cites it.
Leiden's partition depends on its random seed; the default (0), which the code uses by calling sc.tl.leiden without one, decides the outcome, and ten seeds are shown.

The float32 PCA rounds differently with the number of BLAS threads, which changes the neighbor graph and the partition (1, 2 and 4 threads gave three partitions on the same data). BLAS is limited to one thread for the clustering so that the partition does not depend on the machine, a standard choice for a detail of computation; the float64 PCA and 4 threads are shown as perturbations.

outcomes.notes: Default seed, BLAS on one thread. 54 regions have more than 30 clustered cells. Under the criterion's ranking (find_decay on the cluster mean of z-scored cells; faster half 2, 6, 7, 8, 9) the condition holds at FDR 0.05 and 0.01: PAG is overrepresented in cluster 9, VPM in clusters 2 and 8 at 0.05 and in cluster 8 at 0.01, and frontal or limbic regions in slower-half clusters (at 0.01 ACAv5, AId5, ORBl5 and PL2/3 in cluster 0, ORBvl2/3 in 1 and 5, ORBvl5 in 3 and 5). ACAd5 (both thresholds) and PL5 (0.05) are also overrepresented in the faster-half cluster 2. Under the ranking by the pooled baseline-subtracted trace of Fig. 4G (faster half 1, 6, 7, 9, 10) VPM is in no faster-half cluster, and the condition fails at both thresholds. Over ten Leiden seeds the criterion's ranking holds in 8 seeds at 0.05 and 7 at 0.01, the pooled ranking in 3 and 2, and all four combinations in 2 (seeds 4 and 8); every failure is the VPM part, while PAG and frontal hold in every seed. Chance is 1/11 here against the paper's 1/12. Changed from reproduced after verification round 1, and kept: the VPM part depends on the ranking and on the partition.
deviations: With 11 clusters the faster half is taken as the 5 fastest by find_decay.
Leiden seed and BLAS threads as for fig4de-response-clusters; ten seeds shown.

outcomes.notes: Spearman correlation across 11 clusters between Pre decay time and the Pre to Ketamine change is -0.273 (p = 0.42) for the cosine distance and -0.409 (p = 0.21) for the absolute difference over 1 to 2 s. The largest changes are in clusters 0 and 10 (cosine distance 1.171 and 0.754, Pre decay 0.31 and 0.18 s); of the two slowest clusters, 4 changes by 0.622 and 5 by 0.139. Over ten Leiden seeds no correlation is positive with p < 0.05 (rho -0.297 to 0.224 for the cosine distance, -0.486 to 0.248 for the difference).
deviations: Ketamine is series 23 to 32 (10 series, code), where table S3 gives 64 Ketamine puffs (8 series); the criterion names this conflict and follows the code.

outcomes.notes: 35 regions pass at the d' threshold 1.3 and 31 at 2. The median over regions of the bootstrap median change in rise time is +0.0001 s (Ketamine 23 to 32) or -0.0030 s (22 to 32) under every setting, within one 10 ms bin of zero. The Pre median rise is below 0.1 s in 32 of 35 and 30 of 31 regions. The more-than-30 and at-least-30 rules give the same regions. In the code's weighting a cluster without a value (peak after 750 ms) adds zero; that weight averages 0.089 of a region in Pre and 0.246 under ketamine. With the weights renormalized over clusters with a value, with Pre from series 11 to 20 only (20 replicate puffs, as Ketamine), or both, the change is +0.0065, -0.0040 and +0.0040 s, all within one bin, and the Pre rise is below 0.1 s in 31 to 35 regions. The regional values depend on the partition (clustering of fig4de-response-clusters, BLAS on one thread).
deviations: The code skips cluster 11; this clustering has clusters 0 to 10, so none is skipped.
Bootstrap seed 0 is a standard choice.
The renormalized weights and the 10-series Pre set are verification controls, not the paper's method; the code's nansum weighting decides the outcome.

outcomes.notes: The median of the pooled bootstrapped decay changes is -0.162 s (threshold 1.3, code series), -0.158 s (Methods-literal series), -0.165 and -0.161 s at threshold 2. The Ketamine median decay is shorter in 33 of 35 regions (threshold 1.3) and 31 of 31 (threshold 2). Part of the shortening comes from the code's weighting, in which a cluster without a decay adds zero and which drops 0.246 of the weight under ketamine against 0.087 in Pre. Renormalized weights give -0.124 s (29 of 35 regions shorter), Pre from series 11 to 20 only -0.083 s (31 of 36), and both -0.058 s (26 of 36): the decay still shortens under every control, by 0.36 to 0.77 of the main change.

Median Pre decay of the frontal and limbic regions (ACAd, ACAv, AIv, ILA, MOp, MOs, ORBl, ORBm, ORBvl, PL) is 0.473 s at threshold 1.3 (0.513 s at 2, without MOp), against 0.301 s for the midbrain regions MRN, NPC, PAG and SCig; VPM (0.557 s) and MD (0.571 s) lie above the median of all regions (0.433 s).

NMF (sklearn, solver mu, random_state 1, as the code) of the mean of the deposited pre- and postinfusion train-half spectrograms (458 channels, 7 patients, 65 frequencies by 28 times, 0 to 1.37 s), positive and negative parts each with k factors. Held-out explained variance (test half against the train reconstruction, as nmf_k_determination) is 0.466 at six factors (0.4655 under three other seeds), within 0.47 +- 0.047. Gains in held-out R2 are 0.081 from 2 to 4 factors, 0.056 from 4 to 6 and 0.015 from 6 to 8; the largest drop in marginal gain puts the elbow at six, the farthest point from the chord of the 2-to-38 curve at eight. The held-out R2 keeps rising slowly after six factors, to 0.507 at 22, so the elbow depends on the rule; the paper picks it by eye.
deviations: Starts from the paper's deposited z-scored, train/test-averaged spectrograms (sub-H_ses-sgramPerChannel); the spectrograms are not recomputed from the raw iEEG.

Method details from the paper's code (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14920570, analyze_airpuff_ieeg_sgram_load_allpt.py and decode_utils.py get_nmf and nmf_k_determination): training array the mean of the pre- and postinfusion train halves, k from 1 to 19 per sign, R2 of the test half against the train reconstruction.

The paper picks the elbow by eye ("A clear elbow in the reconstruction error plot was identified", Methods, Factorization). It is assumed to be where the marginal gain drops most, the standard discrete elbow; the chord rule gives eight.

outcomes.notes: The six-factor NMF above, applied to the test half of each session, gives back the deposited loadings exactly (values and the channels below the 0.1 threshold on the pre/post mean). Factor 1 (a rise peaking 0.20 s after the puff) has loadings 0.508 before and 0.318 during infusion (260 channels), factor 2 (a fall peaking at 0.41 s) 0.354 and 0.214 (185 channels), all within tolerance. Mixed-effects model of infusion against the mean of pre and post, grouped by patient (7), FDR over six factors: coefficient -0.125 (corrected p = 2.6e-05) and -0.115 (5.5e-08). Factor 3 also falls (corrected p = 0.016); factors 0, 4 and 5 do not change. The deposited loadings give the same table.
deviations: Loadings, threshold and model from the paper's code (decode_utils.compare_nmf_loadings_by_condition, comparison prepost, statsmodels mixedlm); the figure numbers of the factors follow the deposited factor files (sub-H_ses-sgramNMFFactors), as the deposit's order is not the code's order by peak time (its factors 2 and 3 are swapped).

outcomes.notes: Deposited per-trial Yeo7 network spectrograms (sub-H_ses-sgramPerYeoPerTrial, six networks, 153 to 214 paired trials from 5 to 7 patients). mne permutation_cluster_1samp_test on infusion minus preinfusion, trials paired by patient and trial number, cluster-forming threshold p = 0.01 two-sided, 512 permutations: limbic, ventral attention and somatomotor networks each have a cluster at p = 1/512, corrected p = 0.0039 (below 0.01) under three permutation seeds; frontoparietal, default and dorsal attention are not significant (corrected p 0.038 to 0.12). The regional part of the statement is not tested; the criterion is decided by the networks.

findings.statement: The spike times of every one of the 9554 units are stored in no particular order (about half of successive differences are negative); NWB expects them ascending. Sorted, they agree with the stimulus table: the population response 0 to 200 ms after each puff is 0.03 to 0.19 z in every session and -0.03 to 0.003 at onsets shifted by 1.5 s.

The animal excluded from the paper's Figure 5 and 6 analyses (Harderian gland secretion) is not identified in the dandiset or the paper. Removing sub-1, sub-3 or sub-5 each leaves 11 sessions from 9 mice; only removing sub-5 also leaves 7 tone sessions from 7 mice as table S3 reports, and several outcomes depend on the choice.

Question for the paper's authors. Which animal was excluded from the cross-puff and population analyses (Figs. 5 and 6, fig. S34)? This attempt assumes sub-5 (both sessions), the only choice that gives the 7 tone sessions from 7 mice of table S3; fig6d, fig6h, figs34d and figs34g change outcome if sub-1 or sub-3 was excluded instead.

Question for the paper's authors. Fig. 4B and 5B normalize each condition's mean eye-closure trace by its own maximum in analysis.py; is that the normalization behind the reported reduction? Without it, or with both conditions divided by the Pre maximum, the late closure of the recorded mice does not differ between Pre and Ketamine (0.026 [-0.030, 0.082]).
Tone series are in 9 sessions from 8 mice, where table S3 reports 7 sessions from 7 mice, and 9 sessions also hold light stimuli (240 to 248 per session) that the paper does not describe.

The ketamine infusion time in each file is described as approximate and falls 94 to 420 s after the code's ketamine onset (30 s after the last puff of series 20); with the code's onset, the tenth pre-infusion tone series counts as post-infusion.
867 of 9554 units carry the region label NA, and the files give no description of the region labels beyond the acronyms.
DANDI 001326 holds no eye closure; the recorded mice's eye closure is in DANDI 001347, with no file for sub-3_ses-20230225, sub-5_ses-20230706 or sub-5_ses-20230822, and with no tone events.

In DANDI 001347 the behavior-rig files hold only an eye-closure trace and an experiment id, with no drug, dose, pressure or injection label, and the human P50 files label trials only as pre and post. The conditions come only from the session lists of the paper's code (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.14920570).

The recorded-mouse eye-closure files of DANDI 001347 (sub-m<mouse>-<recording>) carry no identifier of the 001326 sessions; the link comes from the paper's conversion script and a clock fit to the series onsets.
Lick data (fig. S4), participant reports (Fig. 1F) and CADSS scores (Fig. 2D, fig. S14G) are not in DANDI 001347 or the code archive.

Table S3 gives a saline late eye closure of 0.34 for fig. S2C; the data give 0.203 while reproducing the table's t value (4.951) exactly, so the reported mean appears inconsistent with the reported test.

Table S3 gives 64 Ketamine puffs per cluster for Fig. 4G (8 series), while analysis.py takes series 23 to 32 (10 series); the recorded-mouse files of DANDI 001347 store a Ketamine range of series 23 to 30, which matches the table.

The coupling loop of analysis.py plot_coding_dimension_early_late takes the windows before puff series 1 to 10 and 23 to 32 whatever the stimulus, so the tone coupling of fig. S34H is computed before puff series, not before tone series as the Methods say; only that version shows a significant fall here.

In the 9 sessions with tones and lights, light or tone onsets fall in the 30 s before 14 of the 30 puff series that the baseline timescale and coupling analyses use (Pre 4 to 9 and 14, 16, 20; Ketamine 24, 28, 29, 30, 32), and in sub-1_ses-20230226 and sub-3_ses-20230225 light onsets fall in every odd 50 s post-series window. The paper does not mention the lights or say whether these windows were excluded.

The "Ketamine infusion start" of every file falls exactly 5.0 s before the first puff of series 21 (series 23 starts 235 to 266 s after it), so the stored infusion time appears to be placed from the puff schedule; its description says only that it is approximate.

The derived human files (sub-H) hold the inputs of the paper's factor and cluster analyses, and an NMF recomputed from sub-H_ses-sgramPerChannel with the paper's code settings gives back the deposited loadings exactly. The factor order of sub-H_ses-sgramNMFFactors is not the code's order by peak time (its factors 2 and 3 are swapped), and the files do not say which order the figures use.

disagreements.reason: Without normalization, Pre minus Ket = 0.026 [-0.030, 0.082]. With each condition divided by its own maximum it is 0.308 [0.243, 0.373]; divided by the Pre maximum it is -0.033. The outcome depends entirely on dividing each condition's trace by its own maximum. Only 10 of the 13 sessions are in 001347.

Pre accumulation is above 0 in every reading. Without normalization, Ketamine accumulation (0.040 [0.012, 0.067]) neither includes 0 nor lies below the Pre mean. It meets the criterion only under per-condition max normalization.
11 clusters, which is within +-1, but 7 of the 12 sizes are outside tolerance and the 12th is missing. Only 1 cluster is persistent where the criterion needs 3.

At FDR 0.05 PAG is in a fast cluster, VPM in cluster 2 (5th fastest of 11), frontal regions in slow clusters; at 0.01 VPM is only in a slow-half cluster. The fast/slow split ranks clusters by decay of cluster_means, while the Fig. 4G cell uses cluster_trace; under the latter VPM's cluster leaves the faster half and figs31b would fail at both thresholds (problem 6). The chance level is 1/11 against the paper's 1/12 (problem 12).

Holds with the code's 3 to 4 s target window, q = 0.0056 to 0.040, under pooled variance and unit-vector scaling. Fails in every session reading with the Methods 5 to 6 s window and per-unit variance (q = 0.105 to 0.113).
q >= 0.05 with the Methods window. With the code window and per-unit variance, q = 0.023, 0.031, 0.048, so the absence fails.

tauP model best in 22 of 24 readings; saturation is best for sub-3 with the code window and pooled variance, by 0.001 to 0.006. The variance explained is computed on the whole Ketamine half, series plus 25 to 70 s afterwards, where the criterion asks for the Ketamine puff-series segment only (problem 1).

7/7 areas pass with the notebook's mean-to-mean comparison with puff 2. Under the criterion's wording (the interval above the puff-2 value), some areas fail, e.g. OLF with the code window (lower bound 0.048 against 0.164), HPF and MB. Most still pass.

Pre vs Ket q <= 0.002 everywhere, and means within tolerance with first-puff projections. Post vs Ket fails without sub-1 (q = 0.051), and under the Methods-literal epochs. The persistent dimension is trained on the same Pre series it is scored on while Ketamine is out of sample; no held-out check was run (problem 10).

Without sub-5, both ways of combining series pass (p <= 0.016) with means within tolerance. Without sub-1 or sub-3, per-series fits fail (p 0.34 to 0.56), driven by degenerate fits: the exponential fit is unbounded and degenerate per-series fits (Ketamine b = 833 s and 1.71 s) enter the session means while the notebook reports "failed fits 0". The autocorrelation is taken without subtracting the mean, which can bias the comparison (problem 2).

Within-region change 0.0063, p = 0.052; between-region change -0.0001, p = 0.89. The RSP (9/10) and ORB (5/7) increases hold, but the Ketamine window starts at the code's onset, 94 to 420 s before the file's infusion start, where the Methods say "10-minute period following the onset of ketamine infusion"; no variant using the file's infusion time was run. The claims file's choice of onset is itself a questionable reading of the paper (problem 3).
RSP has the largest pooled rise at 5 and 10 min. Per-session rises 7/9 at 5 min, but only 5/9 at 10 min (the notebook prints 5 of 10, counting sub-7, which has no value, in the denominator).

entries.name: 001326-kauvar-2025
entries.title: Brain-wide mouse electrophysiology during eyepuffs and ketamine (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001326, which holds Neuropixels recordings of 13 sessions from 10 mice during eyepuff and tone series before and after ketamine, and the behavior in dandiset 001347. The first notebook covers the response clusters and their regional distribution, regional rise and decay times, the emotion-like population dimension and its first-order model, the fast and persistent coding dimensions with their baseline timescale and coupling, the tone responses, and the resting correlation structure and spectra. The second covers the eye closure of the recorded mice, the behavior-only mouse drug, dose, pressure and muscimol experiments, and the eye closure of four non-implanted participants, from dandiset 001347. The third covers the human iEEG factor analysis and the network cluster tests, from the derived spectrograms deposited in dandiset 001347.

entries.title: Eyepuff affect under ketamine in humans and mice (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001347, which holds the human eyepuff behaviour, the iEEG recordings of seven participants with spectrogram products aggregated across them, and the mouse eyepuff behaviour, and on dandiset 001326, which holds the mouse Neuropixels recordings. It tests the eye-closure effects of ketamine and other drugs, the behavioural inclusion of iEEG participants, the NMF factors and cluster tests of the iEEG spectrograms, the human and mouse coding dimensions, timescales and coupling, and the mouse emotion-like dimension.
